samuel1.4.p1.b1.text: Thus the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now the Israelites went out to meet the Philistines in battle and camped at Ebenezer, while the Philistines camped at Aphek.

samuel1.4.p1.b2.text: Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the battlefield.

samuel1.4.p1.b3.text: Why has the LORD brought defeat on us before the Philistines today? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh…

samuel1.4.p1.b4.text: And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

samuel1.4.p2.b1.text: When the ark of the covenant of the LORD entered the camp, all the Israelites raised such a great shout that it shook the ground.

samuel1.4.p2.b2.text: What is this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?

samuel1.4.p2.b3.text: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods?

samuel1.4.p2.b4.text: Take courage and be men, O Philistines! … Now be men and fight!

samuel1.4.p3.b1.text: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent…

samuel1.4.p3.b2.text: The slaughter was very great—thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.

samuel1.4.p3.b3.text: The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

samuel1.4.p4.b1.text: That same day a Benjamite ran from the battle line all the way to Shiloh, with his clothes torn and dirt on his head.

samuel1.4.p4.b2.text: There was Eli, sitting on his chair beside the road and watching, because his heart trembled for the ark of God.

samuel1.4.p4.b3.text: When the man entered the city to give a report, the whole city cried out.

samuel1.4.p5.b1.text: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his gaze was fixed because he could not see.

samuel1.4.p5.b2.text: I have just come from the battle… I fled from there today.

samuel1.4.p5.b4.text: Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are both dead, and the ark of God has been captured.

samuel1.4.p6.b1.text: As soon as the ark of God was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his chair…

samuel1.4.p6.b2.text: By the city gate… being old and heavy, he broke his neck and died.

samuel1.4.p6.b3.text: And Eli had judged Israel forty years.

samuel1.4.p7.b1.text: Now Eli’s daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the news of the capture of God’s ark and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband…

samuel1.4.p7.b2.text: She collapsed and gave birth, for her labor pains overtook her.

samuel1.4.p7.b3.text: Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son!

samuel1.4.p7.b4.text: But she did not respond or pay any heed.

samuel1.4.p8.b1.text: The glory has departed from Israel

samuel1.4.p8.b2.text: And she named the boy Ichabod…

samuel1.4.p8.b3.text: “The glory has departed from Israel,” she said, “for the ark of God has been captured.”
